quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How much stopping power does a motorcycle's front brake provide?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter so the brake applies when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle in front of you. Increase this distance if conditions are bad.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the road is very slippery because oil from cars has not washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for better traction. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person age 21 or older legally considered intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.06 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when taking a long trip?

options.text: Try to minimize the number of rest breaks.
Use artificial stimulants like caffeine if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a rest break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue follows when they wear off.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
It does not matter which portion of the lane you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center portion of your lane. This keeps you away from the passing vehicle and reduces the risk of a collision.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a good traction surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you accidentally lock the rear brake on a good traction surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: What may cause a wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Brakes that are not working properly
A balanced load
Excessive wind

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn just your head.
Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your shoulders.
Turn your entire body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When making a turn, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to get split up.
Riders will reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders will reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Close group riding has benefits: it uses less road space, is easier to see, and groups stay together better. However, riding close does not help you reach your destination faster.

questions.question: What is NOT required for effective eye or face shield protection?

options.text: Able to fasten securely.
Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
Free of scratches.
Able to allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, fasten securely, allow clear side views, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed. It should NOT be so tight that glasses cannot be worn.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire regains traction. Then re-apply the brake.

questions.question: Why should you ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass a vehicle on the left?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It will give you the best chance of spotting hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It will place you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will give you the best chance of spotting hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This increases your view of the next lane and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: When leaning in a curve, your tires have less traction. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes more smoothly and gradually than on a straightaway.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time and apply extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but mainly focus on swerving.
Not perform either action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good traction to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the lead rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: Which of these helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Using only the front brake
Using both brakes
Using the center lane
Maintaining or increasing your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and use both brakes. Avoid sudden movements. Stay out of the center lane and follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: What should you do to react faster to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift to neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
They make objects look closer than they actually are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you. They also make objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice using them so you understand how they work.

questions.question: What gives you maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully to stop in a straight line. Do not lock either wheel. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Try to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve separately, not at the same time. You can brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both actions together.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. If you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting a car.
